hints: A building is visible from a viewpoint when no taller building blocks the line of sight, according to the problem's height rule.
For each query interval, the buildings' relative height records determine visibility.
Use a range maximum structure to skip groups that cannot contribute a visible building.
analogy: From the chosen viewpoint, a building stays visible only while it sets a new height record.
example: Looking across heights 2,5,3,7, the visible record heights are 2,5,7.
complexity: O((n+q) log n) if each visible building is found by a tree search; O(n) tree space.
algorithm: Precompute a next-greater index for every position with a monotonic stack. For each query [a,b], repeatedly jump to the next index after the current record height whose height is strictly larger, stopping at b. Binary-lifting jump pointers let each query skip many visible-record transitions.
correctness: A building is visible exactly when its height exceeds every earlier height in the queried interval; the next-greater chain lists precisely these successive record highs.
